T-001's Test Type field (tasks.md:271-273) states 'Integration (real file read) for the three-element wording check (AC-001) and the absence checks (AC-004...AC-007, bootstrap leg)', grouping AC-004-007 under 'integration'. But acceptance-tests.md's own per-row Test Matrix -- the exact source this field claims to restate ('per acceptance-tests.md's own per-row typing', tasks.md:271) -- classifies TEST-004/TEST-005/TEST-006/TEST-007 as 'unit (literal-absence, both skills)' (acceptance-tests.md:14-17), not integration. A literal-absence check reading one static file (SKILL.md) for the absence of a substring targets a single module/file boundary and involves no second system component, so it fails this check's own definition of an integration test ('must involve at least two system components') independently of the acceptance-tests.md contradiction. T-002's Test Type field (tasks.md:425-427, 'matching T-001's typing for the wording elements ... (integration, real file read / ...)') inherits the identical mislabeling by reference for its own AC-004-007 ship-leg absence checks (tasks.md:466-473). A downstream implementer following this field could build integration-weight test scaffolding for what is scoped and specified elsewhere as a lightweight unit-level literal-absence check, or conflate it with the genuinely-integration presence check (AC-001/AC-002), losing the per-skill failure-isolation acceptance-tests.md:91 requires ('Report per skill').

No task carries Risk: high or Risk: critical (tasks.md:243,394,538,608,666), so the check's mandatory trigger is absent.
